parameters.content:
## 1 Brief and source
Basic Auth form -> run folder -> disclaimer must equal the rulebook's -> source.mp4 (upload, or https link) -> beats parsed and checked with /reframe.

## 2 Scripts
Rulebook -> LLM (2 hooks x 3 lengths, 3 b-roll shots each, structured output) -> shape check.

## 3 Compliance
Hard word list (/lint) on lines and shots; a judge LLM rules on the lines only (shots are pre-approved). Rewrite once, lint again, drop. A shot with a word-list hit is dropped.

## 4 Look line (spec 4.3 part 1)
Vision on the middles of S1, S3, S5; one retry if the word list hits; then the rulebook's look_fallback. The brief's Look overrides.

## 5 B-roll
Dry run: stand-in clips copied to runs/<id>/broll/ (12 files). Live (pods + /api/broll): disabled stub, the toolkit side is not deployed. Run stops at '→ 12b: render', which receives the whole run state (with `slots`).

# 4 Render and QA
One version at a time through `/render` (stand-in or real voice), `/check`, `/transcribe` (the brand as a hotword, the line as the script to compare with), `/frames` of the last frame and a vision read of the end card's disclaimer. QA reasons merge as docs/api.md says; a render error makes that version `failed` and the loop goes on. One at a time because the service renders one at a time (an HTTP node with many items fires them all at once); a render that times out here leaves the service rendering and the next request queues behind it.

# 5 Contact sheet and approval
`/sheet` (green PASS or red FAIL on each cell), then the approval. **First contact is Telegram** (credential `telegram-demo`, chat id read from `data/config/telegram.json`): the sheet as a photo with the summary, then Send and Wait with two buttons. **Approve passed** approves every passed version and rejects the rest; **Review** sends the link of the approval form (the Wait node below: ticks per version, override notes) and goes on into it. If Telegram fails at any step the error goes to run.json (`telegram_error`) and the form takes over. Wait limit 7 days on both; no answer = expired (run.json says which channel), nothing packaged. A failed version can be ticked in the form only with a note `VERSION: why`. The form URL and the sheet link are in run.json.

# 6 Package
`/package` with approved items (and their notes), rejected items with the reason, and the run's facts (mode, times, costs, link, CTA). Stand-in b-roll: no upload (the media service has no R2 environment yet). A built package sends the done message on Telegram (run, counts, cost per asset, turnaround, folder); nothing approved or an expired approval sends a one-line message saying so. A message that cannot be sent is logged in run.json as `telegram_done` (`sent`, `failed: ...` or `skipped: no chat id`) and never fails the run. A failed package ends the run in error (error workflow); nothing approved or an expired approval ends it normally. The answer goes into run.json.

# 7 Contact sheet link (public)
GET `/webhook/ad-versions-sheet?run=<id>&token=<32 hex>`. The token (128 random bits, made in Render: plan, stored in run.json) is the only protection: the `/webhook` path is public through the tunnel by design. Wrong or missing token, wrong run: 404. Only `runs/<id>/sheet.jpg` is ever served.
